biography: I started in mobile engineering and spent years shipping software that had to keep working after release. That habit stuck. When something fails in production, I care less about the clever part and more about whether we can see it, measure it, and fix it.

I moved into AI because the interesting problems stopped being the screen and started being the system — retrieval, permissions, evaluation, integrations with tools people already use. At TCS Hungary I work on those problems every day: ServiceNow knowledge, scheduling optimizers, ranking pipelines. The model is rarely the hard part.
I'm also doing an MSc in AI at ELTE in Budapest. Industry work keeps me honest about what ships; research forces me to measure carefully. The Social Attraction PSO paper came out of that overlap.
